description:
Found by defk-52v.3 (examples/lz4_snappy_decode.exs). Inside an Enum.reduce_while (or for reduce:) body, `if done, do: {:halt, {out, s}}, else: (out = put1(out, i); {:cont, {out, s}})` where put1/2 is a kernel that writes out[i] and returns out: the inlined callee copies `out` before its write on EVERY iteration (report: "copy: out is copied before this write: another binding still sees its buffer"), and every copy lives until the kernel returns. Time and memory are quadratic in the loop length. Writing `out[i] = 1` directly in the same branch does not copy, and hoisting the call out of the branch (`out = put1(out, i)` first, then `if done, do: {:halt, ...}, else: {:cont, ...}`) does not copy either.

Reproduction (Mix.install script):

    defk put1(out :: [u8], i :: i64) :: [u8] do
      out[i] = 1
      out
    end

    defk fill(n :: i64) :: i64 do
      out = alloc(u8, n)
      {out, s} =
        Enum.reduce_while(0..(n - 1)//1, {out, 0}, fn i, {out, s} ->
          if i == n - 1 do
            {:halt, {out, s + out[0]}}
          else
            out = put1(out, i)
            {:cont, {out, s}}
          end
        end)
      s + out[1]
    end

Measured: n = 1k 92 us, 10k 12 ms, 40k 202 ms (hoisted: 1, 4, 7 us); 40k holds ~1.6 GB of copies. In the LZ4/Snappy decoder (copy helper per element, 4 MB output) the BEAM was SIGKILLed (exit 137, out of memory): a kernel took the node down, which the runtime contract says it must not.

Likely cause: the "read after the write" test for an inlined callee's array parameter sees the caller's `out` read by name in the other branch of the enclosing if (or in the next iteration through the accumulator), although the caller rebinds `out` to the result. The direct-write path already handles this case.

Done when: the reproduction copies nothing (fast-path report has no copy note for fill/1, timing linear), a test covers a helper call in one branch with a read in the other, and docs/language.md Copies says how a helper call in a branch behaves. Separately consider a bound on the memory a kernel's copies may hold (a copy in a loop that keeps every buffer until return can exhaust memory).

comments.text: Memory bound for copies split out to defk-4b2 (not done here): every copy/alloc is an owned slot kept until return, so a per-iteration copy that remains legitimate still grows without bound; options and reasoning in the ticket.

Fixed on branch defk-33b/helper-in-branch-copy (a162b96). Cause: lib/defk/compiler.ex nested/1 gave every nested block env.out = env.nest, the enclosing statement's live set plus everything the statement reads, so an if/cond/case arm saw the reads of its sibling arms as live. In the reproduction the if's nest held the reduce_while accumulator out's {id, buf}; inline/4 copies that into the callee's live set (outer), and the callee's parameter binding has a new id but the same buf, so before_write's shared?/2 copied on every iteration. A direct out[i] = 1 escaped only because shared? ignores the binding's own id. Fix: nested/2 takes the block; for a block that is exactly one arm of an if, cond or case in the current statement (arm?/2), out = env.live (read after the statement) + what the statement reads outside the alternatives (taken/2 prunes sibling arms; conditions, case subjects and patterns kept). Loop and fn bodies (run again) keep env.nest. Refines all copy decisions (callee writes, direct writes, hoist, accumulator init), never removes a genuine read. Tests (test/value_semantics_test.exs, 'a helper call in one branch (defk-33b)'): the reproduction plus if/cond/case arms in reduce_while, the hoisted form, for reduce: with a read in a branch after the call: no copy note, no defk_copy_ in the C, agreement properties, forced yields. Negatives still copying and agreeing: array bound outside the loop rebound in a branch (next iteration sees the old one), read after the if, read later in the same statement, alias of the accumulator read after the call. Reproduction before: copy note on fill/1, 1k 87 us, 10k 10 ms, 40k 135 ms; after: no note, 40k 1-2 us, 4M 0.1-0.3 ms (load ~25). Docs: language.md Copies, performance.md 6.15, lz4_snappy_decode.exs comments (workaround kept). Memory bound split to defk-4b2. for reduce: cannot return an array from a branch (array-in-branch), so its branch form is not expressible; covered via a read in a branch after the call.

title: [BUG] A helper kernel that writes and returns an array, called in one branch of a loop body whose other branch reads the array, copies the whole array every iteration and keeps every copy
